A1.justification: Both complete 25-page PDFs describe the same CLIPTTA work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original closed-set and open-set adaptation experiments, component ablations, robustness analyses, and hyperparameter studies in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses, including benchmark results, ablations, and repeated-run accuracy estimates.

M1.justification: The soft contrastive loss, marginal-entropy regularization, class-wise confident memory, and Outlier Contrastive Exposure loss are unchanged. Section 3 retains the same adaptation procedure and objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same corruption, domain-shift, coarse-grained, fine-grained, and open-set coverage. Appendix C preserves the same datasets and SVHN/Places365 OOD pairings, including corrupted counterparts.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding main-text and appendix experiments. The same entropy-based methods, CLIPArTT/WATT, TPT/TDA, and specialized open-set methods participate in their respective comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same ViT-B/16 backbone, non-episodic protocol, batch sizes, Adam learning rate, adaptation iterations, preprocessing, and evaluation metrics. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component ablation in Table 4, text-encoder analysis in Table 7, robustness analyses in Figures 4–6, and hyperparameter and batch-size studies in Figure 7 and Tables 17–18.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 and Table 16 retain accuracy means and 95% confidence intervals over three random initializations. Neither the repeated-run information nor the uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains CLIPTTA's corruption accuracies of 80.7, 52.6, and 41.1, while Table 3 retains 67.6 accuracy, 97.7 AUC, and 9.7 FPR95 for CLIPTTA + OCE.

T1.justification: Propositions 3.1–3.2 and the gradient and OCE derivations in Appendix A are unchanged. Equation relocation, spacing, and revised cross-reference wording do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about contrastive adaptation, robustness to collapse and pseudo-label drift, and open-set performance. The rephrased introductory question preserves the existing scope of contrastive VLMs such as CLIP.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations of robustness and OOD detection, and text-encoder specialization tradeoffs are retained. The conclusion still identifies global text-image interactions as a limitation and real-time adaptation as future work.

D1.justification: Implementation details, baseline hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, and the two NVIDIA V100 32GB GPU disclosure are unchanged. Both PDFs embed the same source-code repository link.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the 53-item bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the distinction from entropy-based TTA and earlier contrastive approaches.

P1.justification: v2 lightly rephrases the introductory research question, changes Appendix cross-references to Sec., updates author affiliations, and replaces the under-review footer with NeurIPS 2025 conference information. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from the top to the bottom of page 7, Equation 9 moves onto page 7, and surrounding text reflows. The research question becomes a separate italicized block. Figures, table structures, and captions retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 makes limited editorial and layout adjustments while retaining the same methods, proofs, empirical evidence, uncertainty reporting, reproducibility details, and limitations, including the appendices. These changes do not materially improve or impair the paper's clarity or scientific support.
